alignments.note: Noun; the following verbless clause writes no subject of its own and the ASV supplies 'It' for the referent this noun denotes, so both realizations belong to this one morpheme's discontinuous unit, headed on the first English occurrence (rule 25, which extends the resumed-subject reading to a written common noun and directs that such a pronoun not be marked added or folded into the predicate). The competing reading marks t005 added under rule 20's impersonal-'it' clause; that clause governs an 'it' no morpheme licenses, as in 'It is enough', and here the verse writes the referent.
